plan_a_advantages: More consistent volume of easy runs
Focus on hill work, which is relevant to trail running
plan_b_advantages: Incorporates interval training for speed development
Includes a dedicated long run for building endurance and trail-specific durability
reasoning: Plan B is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates more targeted workouts like interval sessions designed to improve threshold and aerobic power, which are crucial for faster trail running. Plan A, while consistent, relies heavily on longer, easier runs and hill work, which, while beneficial for endurance, don't directly address the speed component. Plan B’s structured approach with interval training and a dedicated long run will provide a more effective stimulus for improving speed and efficiency on the trails. Furthermore, the inclusion of cross-training helps to reduce impact and prevent overuse injuries, a key consideration for trail runners.
